note: Vanilla generic slot items have no real product, so no published mass exists for them. Each row maps a vanilla placeholder to the researched real device it stands for, and carries that device's published mass. Written by hand and reviewed; it is a judgement of what a placeholder represents, so it is stated here rather than inferred in code.

sources.title: AEE placeholder mapping: vanilla slot items to their real analogue

items.note: Vanilla ItemGPS has no real product. It stands for a handheld military GPS, and the researched analogue is the Garmin Foretrex 701 at 0.088 kg (see device_mass.json, Garmin product page).
Vanilla NVGoggles has no real product. It stands for a monocular image-intensifier goggle, and the researched analogue is the AN/PVS-14 at 0.35 kg (L3Harris product page, see device_mass.json).

Vanilla ItemMap has no real product. A folded field map in a case weighs a small fraction of a kilogram; the value is the lightest band of the carried small kit and is recorded as an analogue rather than a maker figure.
Vanilla ItemCompass has no real product. A lensatic compass is of the order of a tenth of a kilogram with its case.
Vanilla ItemWatch has no real product. A service wristwatch is of the order of 60 g.

items.item: ItemRadio (manpack radio, carried in a pouch)
items.note: Vanilla ItemRadio has no real product. It stands for a handheld or manpack combat radio, and the researched analogue is the AN/PRC-152A at 1.1 kg (L3Harris datasheet, see kit_mass.json).
Vanilla Binocular has no real product. The researched analogue is a 10x42 binocular at 0.695 kg (maker spec, see device_mass.json).
Vanilla MineDetector has no real product. A military metal detector is of the order of 3 kg complete; recorded as an analogue.

Vanilla ToolKit has no real product. ACE states its own ToolKit at 4.0 kg in units of 100 g (ACE_common config mass 40 is not held; ACE publishes 4.0 kg for the toolkit), and the engine gives the vanilla ToolKit mass 80 in slot-space. Recorded as an analogue.

leads.why: The engine gives every item an ItemInfo mass, but it is a slot-space value rather than a mass (FirstAidKit 8, H_HelmetB 30, V_PlateCarrier1 80). It is identity evidence and never a value source.
